findings.claim: An explicit --path is now the fallback when stdin has no usable cwd; without --path bad stdin stays quiet, as row r2 requires.
--json prints {behind, concepts, nudge} and is refused with --format claude (exit 2).
The explanation page now says the briefing's hook prints how to install kmctl and only the nudge prints {}.

The --json output is a dict built by hand in the command body, with behind derived there. .claude/rules/pydantic-boundaries.md says an output shape a caller depends on is built as a typed object, not assembled as a dict, and every other result verb here prints json.dumps(asdict(dataclass)). Give Nudge a behind field (or a small frozen dataclass for the JSON shape) and print json.dumps(asdict(found)), so a renamed key breaks at the type gate and the shape lives in summary.py with its docstring.

verdict.text: All three round-1 findings are fixed, and I checked each by hand.
The new --path fallback leaves the hook path as it was: without --path, empty or bad stdin still prints nothing.
One new non-blocking nit: the --json output is a dict built by hand rather than a dataclass passed through asdict, which is what the repo's other verbs do and what the boundaries rule asks for.
A plain fix is enough, so no new review round is needed.
I re-ran `loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree: lint, format, tests, integration and eval rows r1 to r6 all pass; "stamp green: b511cadabb0c18b62f07a88245301a2965078e6863cfde8c919b86a928e62933".

I read summary_nudge in src/kmctl/__init__.py, Nudge, nudge and payload_cwd in src/kmctl/summary.py, the new and changed tests in tests/test_summary_nudge.py, the summary nudge section of docs/reference/commands.md, and the explanation paragraph.
Logic: root starts as `path or Path(".")`.
Stdin replaces it when it names a cwd.
A payload with no cwd keeps it.
BadPayload re-raises only when path is None, and then the outer except stays quiet.
That matches the help, the epilog and commands.md.
I tested by hand in a scratch repo made with kmctl init plus kmctl new decision.
`kmctl summary nudge --path REPO --json </dev/null` from / printed behind true, the concept id and the nudge.
A repeat printed nudge null with behind still true.
`--json` with no --path and empty stdin printed the quiet object and exited 0.
A payload with no cwd under `--format claude` printed {}, because the set had already been named.
`--json --format claude` exited 2 and named both options.
Tests: test_nudges_with_an_explicit_path_and_unusable_stdin covers each unusable stdin with --path.
test_quiet_on_unreadable_or_empty_stdin still covers r2 without --path.
The JSON tests check the shape on a nudge, a repeat, a current repo and a failure, plus the refused pair.
The rule and practice for the dict: .claude/rules/pydantic-boundaries.md and the other --json verbs in __init__.py, which use json.dumps(asdict(...)) at lines 127, 334, 454, 817 and others.
The one dict precedent, `schema --json`, prints a name-to-purpose map with no fixed record shape.
f1: resolved.
__init__.py:909 to 916 fall back to an explicit --path on BadPayload, and the tests and my manual run confirm it.
f2: resolved.
The --json option, the refusal with --format claude, the help text and the commands.md row are all in place.
f3: resolved.
The explanation page now tells the two hooks' failure output apart.
f4: open, nit, non-blocking.
The JSON is assembled inline at __init__.py:921 to 929.
Move the shape into the Nudge dataclass (add behind) and print asdict(found), like the sibling verbs.
Nothing else changed outside what the fix summary lists.
